drivingQuestion: How can the mishna both forbid the Chariot to an individual and permit it to a wise one?

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמְרַתְּ בְּרֵישָׁא: וְלֹא בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה בְּיָחִיד, וַהֲדַר אָמְרַתְּ: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה חָכָם וּמֵבִין מִדַּעְתּוֹ!
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara poses a question: «You said in the first clause» of the mishna: «Nor» may one expound «the» Design of the Divine «Chariot by oneself,» which indicates that the topic may not be learned at all, «and» yet «you subsequently said: Unless» he «is wise and understands» most things «on his own,» which indicates that an individual is permitted to study the Design of the Divine Chariot.

segments.he: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אֵין דּוֹרְשִׁין בָּעֲרָיוֹת לִשְׁלֹשָׁה, וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית לִשְׁנַיִם, וְלֹא בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה לַיָּחִיד, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה חָכָם וּמֵבִין מִדַּעְתּוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara explains: «This is what the mishna is saying: One may not expound the» topic of «forbidden sexual relations before three» students, «nor» the «act of Creation before two, nor» may one teach «the» Divine «Chariot to one, unless» that student «was wise and understands on his own.»

moves.about: the first clause forbids the Chariot even alone, the latter permits a wise individual
the numbers refer to students taught: not to three, two, or one unless wise
